title: Cap. VI Arg. 5: Arminius's four decrees — Mediator, believers, means, foresight of users
pass_a_gloss: First, he sets down a decree of giving a Mediator. Second, he adds another, of saving believers and those who persevere on account of this Mediator. Third, of administering the means necessary to faith. Fourth, of saving those whom he foresees will believe and persevere by the benefit of these means. In the three prior it is manifest that no certainty of salvation is caused for a singular person; because they are common, and can equally regard reprobates and elect, as far as the bare form of the decrees.
pass_b_english: First: a decree to give a Mediator. Second: to save believers and perseverers for that Mediator's sake. Third: to administer the means needed for faith. Fourth: to save those he foresees will believe and persevere by those means. The first three cause no certainty of salvation for any one person — they are common, and in bare form can as well cover reprobates as elect.
source_text: Primo, ponit decretum de dando Mediatore. Secundo, adjungit aliud, de salvandis credentibus et perseverantibus propter hunc Mediatorem. Tertio, de administrandis mediis ad fidem necessariis. Quarto, de salvandis illis quos praevidet beneficio horum mediorum crediturus et perseveraturos. In tribus prioribus manifestum est nullam certitudinem salutis singulari personae causari; quia communia sunt, et aeque ad reprobos atque electos spectare possunt, quoad nudam decretorum formam.
